content:
{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Redundant wording in ORR endpoint",
      "quote": "To evaluate the efficacy of pralsetinib compared with compared with investigator’s choice of SOC",
      "page": 35,
      "section": "Table 4",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The phrase 'compared with' is duplicated, which is a typographical error that could cause confusion in the protocol.",
      "fix": "Remove the duplicate 'compared with' to read 'compared with investigator’s choice of SOC'."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inconsistent definition of CBR",
      "quote": "CBR, defined as the proportion of participants who experience a best response of SD with a minimum duration of 6 months, a CR, or a PR",
      "page": 35,
      "section": "Table 4",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The CBR definition requires SD duration of 6 months, but the DCR definition does not specify a minimum duration for SD. This inconsistency may lead to ambiguity in endpoint assessment.",
      "fix": "Clarify whether CBR and DCR use the same SD duration criteria, or specify different definitions clearly."
    },
    {
      "title": "Restrictive tumor tissue requirement may cause enrollment delays",
      "quote": "If no adequate tumor material is available and a new biopsy is not feasible, the participant will not be eligible for enrollment.",
      "page": 45,
      "section": "5.1 Inclusion Criteria",
      "category": "amendment_risk",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "This criterion is very restrictive and may exclude many patients who cannot provide tissue, potentially slowing enrollment and limiting generalizability.",
      "fix": "Consider allowing enrollment based on local RET fusion test results with central confirmation post-enrollment, or provide a waiver process for exceptional cases."
    },
    {
      "title": "Ambiguous CNS metastasis exclusion criteria",
      "quote": "Participant has either CNS metastases or a primary CNS tumor that is associated with progressive neurological symptoms or requires increasing doses of corticosteroids to control the CNS disease.",
      "page": 47,
      "section": "5.2 Exclusion Criteria",
      "category": "advisory",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The criteria do not specify what constitutes 'progressive neurological symptoms' or 'increasing doses' of corticosteroids, which may lead to inconsistent interpretation across sites.",
      "fix": "Define these terms more precisely, e.g., specify a minimum dose increase or a timeframe for symptom progression."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing safety monitoring for pneumonitis",
      "quote": "Participants with a history of pneumonitis of non-infectious etiology within the last 12 months.",
      "page": 47,
      "section": "5.2 Exclusion Criteria",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The protocol excludes patients with recent pneumonitis but does not specify monitoring for pneumonitis during the study, which is a known adverse event for pralsetinib and checkpoint inhibitors.",
      "fix": "Add a safety monitoring plan for pneumonitis, including regular imaging and management guidelines."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inconsistent contraception duration for men",
      "quote": "during the treatment period and for 7 days after the final dose of pralsetinib",
      "page": 45,
      "section": "5.1 Inclusion Criteria",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The male contraception duration is only 7 days after pralsetinib, which may be insufficient given the drug's half-life; also, it is inconsistent with the female duration of 14 days.",
      "fix": "Align male contraception duration with female duration or justify based on pharmacokinetic data."
    },
    {
      "title": "Potential conflict in prior therapy exclusion",
      "quote": "Participant cannot have received any prior anticancer therapy for metastatic disease.",
      "page": 45,
      "section": "5.1 Inclusion Criteria",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "This criterion is clear, but the subsequent allowance for prior adjuvant therapy may be misinterpreted; ensure that 'metastatic disease' is clearly defined to avoid ambiguity.",
      "fix": "Clarify that prior therapy for early-stage disease is allowed, but any therapy for metastatic disease is prohibited."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing safety monitoring for liver function",
      "quote": "Change from baseline in targeted clinical laboratory test results",
      "page": 35,
      "section": "Table 4",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The endpoint mentions 'targeted clinical laboratory test results' but does not specify which tests, and there is no explicit monitoring for hepatotoxicity, which is a known adverse event for pralsetinib.",
      "fix": "Specify liver function tests (ALT, AST, bilirubin) in the safety monitoring plan and include as a secondary endpoint."
    }
  ]
}
